kit_items: Solar panels: 8 × Sun Gold Power 450 W bifacial N-type panels (3.6 kW), included in SGR-8K10E. This matches the 3.4 kW ChatGPT's calculator gives for 10 kWh/day at 4 sun hours.

Inverter/charger with built-in MPPT: Sun Gold Power 8,000 W 48 V 120/240 V split-phase, included. The store says it has two MPPT solar inputs, takes up to 11,000 W of panels, charges at up to 180 A and has Wi-Fi monitoring, so no separate charge controller is needed.

Batteries: 2 × Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2 V 100 Ah server-rack LiFePO4 (10.24 kWh), included. They talk to the inverter over RS485 and are UL1973/UL9540A certified. Add more SG48100P units in parallel to reach ChatGPT's 2-day reserve.

Protection and wiring (comparable SGR-10K20E list; the SGR-8K10E list was cut off in the store data): 300 A DC breaker, 25 A PV breaker, 50 ft PV extension cables, 2/0 AWG battery/inverter cables, Z-bracket mounts. The shopper still needs racking, grounding, an AC disconnect and a panelboard.

Cold-climate option: use self-heating batteries if they sit in an unheated cabin. Sun Gold Power puts self-heating SGH48100T batteries in its 'T' kits (for example SGR-10K25T). Vatrer's heated 48 V 100 Ah sends incoming charge power to heating at or below 32°F and starts charging above 41°F.

unsourced: How many of the SGR-8K10E's 450 W panels can go in series on one solar input. Search snippets suggested a 120–500 V MPPT range and 22 A per input for the SPH8048P inverter, and Voc 35.03 V / Isc 16.05 A / −0.28%/K for the SGN-450-BDG5 panel. If those hold, two strings of 4 would drop below the 120 V minimum in summer heat, two strings in parallel on one input would exceed 22 A, and one string of 8 (about 316 V in cold weather) would fit. I tried the sungoldpower.com product page, offgridstores, shopsolarkits, renewableoutdoors, offgridsource (HTTP 429), and manuals.plus and solartown (HTTP 403). I downloaded the panel datasheet PDF from solaris-shop, but the text extraction step needed an approval I didn't have.
